headline: High: shared filesystem and MCP bridge create prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict risks; no default isolation is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python interfaces, while Mentat reads/writes files and shares state via filesystem. That creates a plausible bridge for attacker-controlled content to flow from A into B as trusted instructions. The interaction is documented only at the profile level, so uncertainty remains, but the pathway exists in default setups.
conditions: IF MemMachine content is routed into Mentat via shared files or MCP messages
IF Mentat parses file content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared workspace handoff between the agents
Route A→B content through a human review step
Add provenance tags to all A-generated files
Restrict Mentat to a read-only input directory
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing middleware between MCP and file inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context and has network egress, while Mentat reads selected files and sends requests to a configured model provider. If both operate on the same workspace or account, sensitive content from A can be exposed through B's file ingestion and outbound API calls. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or files
IF Mentat forwards those files to its model provider
mitigations: Separate A and B into different workspaces
Remove sensitive files from Mentat's command-line inputs
Use a redaction pass before B sees A outputs
Confirm provider-side retention settings for Mentat
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. MemMachine can use MCP and network egress, so if A also writes into the same workspace through MCP or API-driven automation, both agents can mutate shared artifacts without locking. That overlap can corrupt files or git history; uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF MemMachine writes artifacts into the same directory Mentat edits
IF both agents modify git state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Pause one agent while the other commits
Require manual git review before any commit
Use file locks around shared outputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can emit conversational outputs through REST, SDK, or MCP, and Mentat is a coding assistant that can act on file-based inputs. If Mentat treats A's output as authoritative, an error or hallucination in A can cascade into incorrect edits or commits. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Mentat consumes MemMachine output as task instructions or facts
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted
mitigations: Require a review step before Mentat edits files
Ask Mentat to cite source files for every change
Limit A to drafting only, not final instructions
Compare A outputs against original sources
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine is documented as touching long-term user facts and conversational context, while Mentat handles source code and model-provider API keys. If the pair is used on regulated or sensitive codebases, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the two agents' storage and outbound paths. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the mismatch risk is moderate.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are processed by both agents
IF their retention or residency policies differ in deployment
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either agent
Check provider retention settings for Mentat
Keep MemMachine data in a separate tenant
Document data-class handling for both tools
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
